newsitem.title: CROATIA: Apparition brings chaos to Croatian village.
newsitem.headline: Apparition brings chaos to Croatian village.

text.p: Reports that the Virgin Mary appeared in a football field in predominantly Roman Catholic Croatia have turned life upside down in the humdrum village of Gradina, with hundreds of people coming to see the site of the apparition.
"We have lost our peace," sighed Zeljko Teri, president of Gradina soccer club, near which the apparition is said to have occurred. "Our life has completely changed overnight".
The Virgin is reported to have appeared to a group of around 50 children and two teachers on Friday the 13th. Roman Catholic Church officials are refusing any comment on the event.

A notice board at the vicarage said the local priest, who first spoke to the children, has left Croatia to visit Fatima and Lourdes, sites in France and Portugal where the Virgin Mary is believed to have appeared to local people. Meanwhile, Gradina is being overrun with visitors.
"The police don't know how to regulate traffic now, where to have all these cars parked," said the local mayor Zdenko Blazicevic.

Krunoslav Timar, 10, said: "When I came out on the playground I saw everything clearly -- the outlines of her figure, though not the face. She was very large, hovering in the air, way down across the fields."
The apparition, clad in a blue dress and white scarf, swayed slowly and gradually approached the children, he said.
"She didn't speak to us, and when she came closer I started crying and ran away to fetch my mother," Timar said. "When I found her and brought her here she didn't see anything".
Local officials dismissed the notion that the whole thing was concocted to attract crowds and make money.
"If we had wanted to set something up we would have been better organised. Now we don't have enough toilets or wash basins for the pilgrims," Blazicevic said.

But he admitted the town was overwhelmed with offers from people searching for a quick buck. "People want to buy land here, set up hamburger stalls and souvenir shops but it's out of the question. We'll see what time brings."
Zdenka Jeftimija, one of two teachers who saw the apparition, said she did not believe what she saw at first.
"The children looked upset and afraid when they came to my room. Some of them cried so I went out with them just to have a look and calm them down."
But Jeftimija said the silhouette was very large and shone so brightly she had to shield her eyes.
"There are relevant people to look into this. What bothers me is that it's being blown out of proportion now," she said.
Other Gradina residents might disagree.
"We sold over 3,000 beers to the pilgrims last night. That's fantastic," said a waitress at the soccer club cafe.

The visitors, mostly families from the area, go to the playground as soon as they finish work. Up to 1,000 gathered on Wednesday night to watch, sing and pray. Soldiers have pitched a huge army tent in a field in case of rain.
Most pilgrims on Thursday stood in awe and silence near a wooden cross erected in the field after the event.

They stared hard at the skyline of tall aspen trees across the field where a blurred shape, roughly resembling a woman's figure, can be seen in the blue sky shining through the leaves of the trees. Most sighed in amazement when they thought they discerned the Virgin Mary.
"Look, she's holding a baby. And there are angels around her. Oh sweet Jesus," cried a gypsy woman, whose numerous family came in a large van from a nearby town.
Others were already less enthusiastic.

"I hiked over the field to that site. When you come closer you don't see anything - it's just an illusion. When leaves move it looks as if the figure's moving," said Pavle Popsavin, a retired soldier and amateur astronomer.
"And the light they see at night is probably Venus, it's visible from its current position," he said.
